source.question: e-8879
source.value:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071875/assets/56a380b075d10862170ed9c9a45c07dddff3eaef1ea9fb3109a61cc3d27b5ac4.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $y=f(x)$ by $2\pi$ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in[a,b]$ has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,\,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,x\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $y=f(x) = x^2 \geq 0$ for all $x \in \left[0,1\right].$

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\mathbf{r}(x,\theta) = \big\langle x, \: x^2 \cos\theta, \: x^2\sin\theta \big\rangle,
\quad
x \in \left[0, 1\right],
\quad
\theta \in [0,2\pi).
$$

decisions.question: e-12364

source.question: e-12364
source.value:
Notice that $y=e^{x/2} \geq 0$ for all $x \in [0,2].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,(x,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x)=e^{x/2},$ and 

$$
D = \big\{ (x,\theta) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq \theta \lt 2\pi \big\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂x},\,\frac{∂y}{∂x},\,\frac{∂z}{∂x}⟩=⟨1,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨0,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f{f}^{′}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +f{f}^{′}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f{f}^{′},\,-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f=e^{x/2},$ we obtain $f' = \dfrac12 e^{x/2}.$ So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}=⟨\frac{1}{2}{e}^{x},\,-{e}^{x/2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{e}^{x/2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $1$st component of the product is $\dfrac{1}{2}e^x.$

decisions.question: e-12365

source.question: e-12365
source.value:
Notice that $x=\sin z \geq 0$ for all $z \in [0, \pi].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,(z,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(z)=\sin z,$ and

$$
D = \big\{ (z,\theta) \, : \, 0 \leq z \leq \pi , \, 0 \leq \theta \leq 2\pi\big\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂z},\,\frac{∂y}{∂z},\,\frac{∂z}{∂z}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}f⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

  

and

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖ & =\sqrt{(-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+({f}^{′}f)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\text{d}z\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{D}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta \,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\cdot \theta \,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}z \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(z)=\sin z,$ we obtain $f'(z) = \cos z.$ So, finally, we conclude that our expression for the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡z\sqrt{1+(\operatorname{cos}⁡z)^{2}}\,\text{d}z \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$
